title: Kid Rena's style and Shulky following him
summary: Discussion of Kid Rena's high-note style and how Shulky, who followed the band around, played just like him.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Buddy Bolden and Buddy Petit: the trumpet legends

blocks.x: Yeah I've heard about that. I've heard that Renee did a lot of that too.
He did. He was. He was.
He was. And you remember anything about Renee's style when you heard it as you remember him playing? I've heard he played high notes but I wondered if you could tell anything else about his style.
Well I'll tell you who's closer to his style now I think, so my idea is this. That's all right. Just take your time.
What is this band? Shulky. Shulky.

Shulky. Well a couple of other people mentioned it. I was going to ask if it was Shulky. If you listen to Shulky. If you listen to Shulky you hear Renee. People tell me he used to follow the band around.
That's right. Shulky did. And Shulky picked up Renee's style.

But I never heard, he never played such high notes actually. No but he just, he played, Renee was a little higher but the same style that Shulky had, Renee had that same style. When you hear Shulky you hear Renee. It's really true. It's really true that Shulky played just like Renee, kid Renee. I think they, I don't know if Renee taught him or what but I know every time Renee would play his job Shulky would be around.

I think somebody did say he almost took lessons, at least they used to follow the band around. That's right. Shulky did. I think somebody said he maybe even took a couple of lessons or something from him.
I think he did because Shulky had the same style. Anytime Shulky played he'd just say that's Renee played because it sounded just the same
thing. You remember who else was in the band when your father and uncle were in the band?
